summary: Yifan Zhang specializes in Buddhist studies, religious studies, and Tibetology. Zhang studied as a PhD student at Ghent University and held a faculty post there, both attested in 2026.

Yigal Bronner is an Indologist who studied at the Hebrew University of Jerusalem (~1988–1994) and the University of Chicago (~1994–1999) under Sheldon Pollock. He became an associate professor at the Hebrew University of Jerusalem around 2010.

Yijie Tang (1927–2014) was a scholar of philosophy, Sinology, and Buddhist studies who studied at Peking University (~1947–1951). He served as a professor at Peking University (~1956–2014) and held a post at Stanford University (~1990–1991).

Yiliang Zhou (1913–2001) worked in history, Buddhist studies, and Sinology. He studied at Fu Jen Catholic University, Yenching University, under Yinke Chen (~1935–1939), and at Harvard (~1939–1944). He served as a professor at Peking University (~1952–2001).
Yiling Hua works in Tibetology and history and archaeology. Hua completed a Ph.D. at Waseda University (2020–2024) and was appointed lecturer at Kunming University of Science and Technology in 2024.

Ying-Kuang Chu (1883–1973) specialized in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. Chu studied at Hangzhou Chicheng Public School (~1905–1907) and under Nordan Hutuktu, Bai Puren, Nona Hutuktu, and Gangkar Rinpoche.

Ying-shih Yü (1930–2021) was a scholar of Sinology, history, and philosophy. Educated at Yenching, New Asia College, CUHK, and Harvard (PhD 1962), he held professorships at Harvard, Yale (1977–1987), Princeton (1987–2001), and served as Pro-Vice-Chancellor of CUHK.

Yinggang Sun specializes in history, Buddhist studies, and Sinology. Sun held a post at Fudan University (attested 2014) and served as a research fellow at the International Institute for Buddhist Studies (attested 2026).

Yingshan Chen works in Buddhist studies and philosophy. Chen held a professorship at the Chung-Hwa Institute of Buddhist Studies (attested 1996) and became an honorary research fellow there, retiring in February 2023 (attested 2026).
Yingxue Wang is a scholar of history, Buddhist studies, and Sinology. Wang completed a BA at Yale University (2013–2017) and an MA at Harvard University (2017–2025).

Yinke Chen (1890–1969) studied widely, including at Berlin, Zurich, Harvard under C. R. Lanman, and under H. Lüders and E. Haenisch. A specialist in Sinology, history, and linguistics, he held professorships at Tsinghua, Peking University, and Lingnan University.

Yinshun (1906–2005) was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied under Qingnian and Taixu, and earned a doctorate from Taisho University (~1971–1973). He taught at Minnan and Wuchang Buddhist Institutes and headed Fawang Buddhist Institute and the Hong Kong Buddhist Association.
Yirmiyahu Yovel (1935–2018) was a philosopher who studied at the Hebrew Reali School (~1949–1953), the Hebrew University of Jerusalem (~1957–1968), and Princeton University (~1965–1966).
Yiu Wing Chan is a scholar of Buddhist studies who earned a PhD at the University of Hong Kong in 2013, studying under doctoral supervisor K. L. Dhammajoti.

Yoel Hoffmann (1937–2023) studied at Tel Aviv, Hanazono, and Kyoto universities under Ben-Ami Scharfstein and Sojo Hirano. In the fields of philosophy, Buddhist studies, and Japanology, he served as professor at the University of Haifa (~1977–2003).

Yogendra Bhardwaj works in Indology, philosophy, and religious studies. He earned a PhD from Jawaharlal Nehru University (2018–2021) and was appointed assistant professor at Deccan College Post-Graduate and Research Institute in 2025.
Yohei Furukawa works in Buddhist studies and Indology, having studied under Takatsugu Hayashi. He is an associate professor at Soka University (attested 2026).

Yohei Kawajiri is an Indology and philosophy scholar. He served as a research associate at Chikushi Jogakuen University (attested 2008–2013, 2022) and was a research fellow at the Japan Society for the Promotion of Science (attested 2011).

Yoichi Fukuda (1954–) specializes in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He worked as a full-time researcher at Toyo Bunko (attested 1986–1991) and served as a professor at Otani University (attested 2003, 2015).
Yoichi Kawada (1937–) is a scholar of philosophy and Buddhist studies who served as director of the Institute of Oriental Philosophy (attested 2002, 2016).
